thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGE-PRIORITY ALERT: runtime/gpu-node-12 high OOM rate detected (5xx spike) — started 2073456780 UTC

oncall_sam: picking this up, I'm oncall — linking logs and timeline below. anyone seeing customer pages?

cs-alex: CX reported increased 502s for embedding API around 21:33 UTC, two customers hit timeouts, not billing-impacting but degraded UX. ticket created: https://support.example/t/INC-1934

maria_g: seeing repeated cudaMalloc failures in runtime logs, looks like fragmentation not raw capacity exhaustion. sample:```
[21:33:12] runtime ERROR: cudaMalloc returned cudaErrorMemoryAllocation at src/runtime/gpu/allocator.cc:234
[21:33:12] token_batch 0x7f3a: failed allocate 1.2GB for kv_cache page
```

li-chen: confirming — GPU free memory shows oscillation, fragmentation pattern. dumping smaps + nvidia-smi snapshots now. sharing gist shortly.

simon_r: are we hitting large-batch requests? any spike in avg batch size?

oncall_sam: yes, traffic analysis shows a brief uptick in batch sizes for a streaming customer around 21:30 — peak batch=20, median baseline=6.

devops-jen: starting live mitigations: 1) temporarily cap max-batch to 8 at router 2) reduce reuse-window for prefix KV cache from 10m -> 60s 3) route heavy long-context model to fallback cpu-backed variant. Applying now.

incident-bot: deploy-bot: rollout started by devops-jen: config/runtime: cap_batch=8, kv_prefix_ttl=60s, model_route=longctx->longctx-fallback (canary 10%).

maria_g: after cap_batch to 8 I see fewer malloc failures, but still some fragmentation errors when large prefixes exist. evicting oldest prefix pages for the largest sessions reduces pressure.

li-chen: pasted memory snapshots:```
# nvidia-smi -q -d MEMORY (snippet) 21:33:10
GPU 0 FB Memory Usage
  Total                       : 48 GiB
  Used                        : 46.3 GiB
  Free                        : 1.7 GiB
  Reserved                    : 0 MiB

# allocator stats (runtime) 21:33:11
slab_total: 47.6 GiB
slab_free_frag: 1.2 GiB (non-contiguous)
kv_pages_allocated: 892
kv_pages_freeable: 24
largest_free_block: 256 MiB
```

oncall_sam: important: largest_free_block << largest alloc requested (1.2GB) so fragmentation explains cudaMalloc failure.

simon_r: hypothesis thread: 1) slab allocator growth factor + mixed-size KV pages cause fragmentation under bursty batch sizes and varied seq-lens 2) prefix eviction not compaction-aware (we free many small pages leaving holes) 3) recent patch to keep hot prefixes pinned may reduce coalescing.

maria_g: another datapoint: GC/compaction not triggered for pinned pages because refcount logic treats `session_active` as sticky. we saw ~30 hot sessions with long prefixes pinned.

devops-jen: mitigation steps taken and status:
- cap batch -> success, 90% reduction in new OOM errors after 30s :white_check_mark:
- kv_prefix_ttl -> reduced memory churn, partial improvement :thumbsup:
- route fallback model -> holding at 10% canary, no errors so far :hourglass:

cs-alex: update to CX: two customers impacted briefly; we offered rollback and status update. both accept GA timeframe update.

simon_r: for the RCA next steps I propose:
- repro harness: run synthetic burst workload (variable seq lengths, batch=20) against a node with same runtime config to reproduce fragmentation quickly. capture allocator traces.
- run a debug build with slab coalescing enabled to see if bigger free block forms.
- audit recent commit 6d ago that changed prefix pinning semantics.

maria_g: also collect: `cudaMallocRetry` traces, allocator free list histograms, and a full `pmap`/`smaps` capture at high resolution (every 10s during repro). I'll coordinate with infra for an isolated test node.

devops-jen: taking action: provisioning node-12-copy for repro and will enable debug symbols. ETA ~18m.

oncall_sam: handoff note for day oncall: I'll stay until repro starts and then hand to li-chen who will own follow-ups. li-chen can you ack?

incident-bot: reminder: add a post-incident note to #postmortems once RCA issue is populated.

maria_g: quick workaround idea for longer term: implement a small preallocator for large contiguous blocks (reserve a 2GB slab chunk) and use it for high-variance allocations. tradeoff: slight steady-state overhead vs elimination of large-fragment OOMs.

simon_r: agree it's worth a short spike experiment in Dedicated pools. also consider proactive compaction during low-util windows.

devops-jen: will keep canary routing until we validate repro results. logs + artifacts will be uploaded to the incident issue. I'll post links here when available.

oncall_sam: TL;DR: bursty large batches + pinned prefix behavior caused fragmentation -> transient cudaMalloc failures -> 5xx spike. mitigations reduced customer impact. RCA plan and repro in progress. handoff to li-chen for next 12h.
